transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you into the clinic?

I’m here because the new operations manager has been picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. Since then, I can’t seem to leave work at work. I come home wound up and snap at my husband, then I lie awake replaying meetings. And the next day I’m second-guessing routine quality calls I used to make without any trouble.
About how long have you been feeling this way?
About two months now—since the new operations manager started changing the inspection procedures.
Aside from feeling stressed about work, have you been feeling persistently down, depressed, or hopeless?
I’m not sure I’d say depressed or hopeless. I’ve mostly just been keyed up about work.
Aside from work, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other areas of your life, such as your health, finances, or family?
No, not really. It’s mainly the work situation that’s been on my mind.
Before this new manager arrived two months ago, did you experience any issues with anxiety or feeling keyed up like this?
No. I was doing fine before he came in. It started building within a few weeks of the procedure changes, and by the second month it was following me past the workday.
